prototype_status: integrated seeded small-pool target PRNG verified in full battles
initialization: CPU may construct a seeded initial MT state. Upload only the seed-derived 624 uint32 words and index, never observed draws or CPU-selected recipients.
seed_contract: uint32, default 0 shared by independent CPU/GPU executions
kernel_layout: Prefer a per-squad 625-word initial-state input and MT fields in State; do not duplicate seed state into all five character rows.
draw_rules: Small pool n<=5 uses Python random.sample pool algorithm; generate _randbelow(n-i) using getrandbits(n.bit_length()) with rejection.
Keep selected recipient order as well as mask. Reordering random heal recipients changes synchronous effects.
Resolve each random target once per actual CPU-equivalent target resolution. target() and recipient_order() must not independently redraw.
Ordered target-list bounds must include the maximum cardinality of new random target kinds, preserving the 21-recipient encoding limit.
allies_random excludes caster; allies_random_with_debuff includes caster and filters both harmful and harmful_irremovable before sampling.
Expected-mode chance accumulators remain separate from target-selection PRNG. Full random-damage modes are not covered by this prototype.

Generic allies_random:N is lazy for buffs/DoT carriers; reuse the CPU (caster, activation time, raw target) cache. Instant and ordered-list child resolution is eager. Do not label every random target eager.

Check exhausted max_trigger BEFORE any target selection. For non-lazy string targets only, a successful budget probe and actual resolution can be two separate draws. Lists skip the string probe. Empty probes do not consume budget.

Periodic instant registration performs no actual target selection; only an applicable budget probe may sample. from_tick resolves the target anew. Periodic lazy DoT carriers resolve on first reference.
A singleton nonempty sample must still consume the Python rejection draws; an empty pool consumes no draws.
Current recipient_order(kind17) re-evaluates list_target after target(). Replace this with one resolved mask plus captured order, not a definition-global cache that can be clobbered by nested events.

Preserve lazy cache after the first carrier is removed when another same-key carrier is still unresolved. A later activation group must not overwrite an earlier key: lifecycle removed-carrier-cache-survives-later-group proves this.
cleanse_rules: Select oldest harmful instances independently per recipient, using the original list atomically; deduplicate recipient effects.
Only exact harmful polarity is removable; positive fractional limits truncate then still remove at least one; nonpositive or missing limit means all.
Do not emit state-end events or cancel DoT timers on cleanse. Do not clear retained shield/bullet maps on partial stripping.
A stripped scaling DoT carrier falls back to current reference stacks on later ticks; stale captured stacks must not be reused.
gates: Complete repaired v18 regression and checkpoint before changing the combat compiler/kernel.
Verify standalone MT words, small-pool samples, rejection state consumption and final state on GPU.
Port cleanse and random selection; run positive harmful-recipient and real-character cases with identical seeds.
Verify native/PTX complete battles, owned equipment and normal API/UI; keep unsupported effects fail-closed.
